methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $178M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Heron Power is a Series B climate and energy company founded by Drew Baglino that has raised $178M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a universe of 9 private peers and 1 public comparable (Lilium Aviation, LNZA), including same-sector adjacents like KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Amogy across Series C stage.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $178M total raised as a proxy base value and applies a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B progression, yielding $338M. Peer-median analysis references three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables: KoBold Metals at $3.0B, Electric Hydrogen at $1.0B, and Amogy at $700M. The median across these three is $1.0B, with a range spanning $700M to $3.0B. 

Triangulating these two methods produces a valuation range of $287M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median estimate of $669M. The wide spread reflects meaningful uncertainty in peer selection and stage-adjusted multiples within the climate tech sector. Key sensitivities include (1) whether Heron's technology trajectory tracks closer to the lower-stage peers or the $1B+ cohort, and (2) near-term capital efficiency relative to the comparable set. The stage-progression and peer-median approaches diverge substantially, suggesting the true value likely lies within but toward the lower-middle portion of this range pending further operational de-risking.
